name: Muscadet

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Muscadet left on its dead yeast cells, the lees, after fermentation. It gains flavor and texture from them.

notes: Muscadet is made from Melon and has no Muscat-like flavor.
It is light bodied, almost always dry, and has a legal maximum of 12% alcohol.
It is fresh and crisp, with citrus and mineral notes, and is best within three years of release.
Wines kept longer on their lees are slightly fuller bodied.
In cool years the grapes can lack the fruit to balance their acidity.

blurb.text: A Loire Valley AOC for still white wine from the Pays nantais, at the western end of the valley. It is made mainly from Melon, and current rules allow up to 10% Chardonnay.
